description: Protocol versions, unknown fields and types, extensions, and extension_required.

cases.description: auth.scopes is optional: a document with an auth that describes no scope is used (§3.1, §4.7).
scopes_supported is a SHOULD: issuer metadata without it is used (§3.2).
A poppy entry's access is session by default, or signed_in; a value the SDK doesn't know is an absent hint, and another protocol's access says nothing (§3.2).
Before 1.0 every version can break the one before: a document whose major.minor this personal agent doesn't support is not used (§3.1).
An extension this agent does not implement is ignored; the ones it does are declared at the version the company lists (§3.3, §3.4).
An entry of another major version isn't support for this one: nothing is declared.
Operations version 2 is another major version than 3: a company that lists only 2 gets no operations declaration, and leaves approval to itself (Operations 2).
An extension the Company recognizes from the request, such as Mediated Sign-In's grant, is used without being declared in Poppy-Extensions (§3.3, §3.4).
At an endpoint the protocol or an extension defines, extension_required and its extension are in the JSON body (§3.3); the token endpoint returns none.
At an API too, extension_required and its extension are in a JSON body (§3.3, §7).
extension_required is not an access token error: a WWW-Authenticate challenge that names it, with no JSON body, is not read as one (§3.3, §7).
An operation needs terms and no summary (Operations 3); members this version doesn't define are kept.
An operation without terms is not one, whatever its summary says (Operations 3).

input.summary: Exchange the jacket for USD 70.00 more.

cases.description: An entry with a trailing slash does not match: resources compare as exact strings (§3.2, RFC 9728 §3.3).
An entry with a path does not match `https://{domain}` (§3.2).
The host compares ignoring case, and nothing else does (§3.2).
The issuer is found from the domain's protected resource metadata (§3.2): poppy.json needs no auth.issuer when it lists one authorization server.
The domain's protected resource metadata has resource exactly https://{organization.domain} (§3.2); a trailing slash is another resource.
With several authorization servers in the domain's protected resource metadata, auth.issuer is required (§3.1, §3.2).
With several authorization servers, auth.issuer names the one Personal Agents use (§3.1, §3.2).
auth.issuer MUST be one of the domain's authorization servers (§3.1).
With one authorization server, auth.issuer, if present, MUST name it (§3.1).
A Company with no issuer can only be browsed as a website (§3.2): its domain publishes no protected resource metadata, and poppy.json lists only web.
The metadata's issuer matches auth.issuer character for character: a trailing slash is another issuer (§3.2).
An issuer with a path has its metadata at the RFC 8414 §3.1 URL: the well-known path between host and path (§3.2).
organization.domain is the host that served the document, compared ignoring case only: a leading www. is not ignored (§3.1).
A document speaks for the host that serves it after redirects: one served by a provider's host can't name the company's domain (§3, §3.1).
A redirect may change host, but only a document at /.well-known/poppy.json, with no query, speaks for a domain: an upload elsewhere on it does not (§3, §9.3).
The last URL has the well-known path and no query (§3).
www.example.com redirects to example.com, which serves a document naming example.com: it speaks for example.com (§3).
Domains are compared ignoring case (§3.1).
poppy.json is a newer version's document and links the version this agent implements: that version's document, on the same host, is used (§3.4).
Neither poppy.json's version nor any it links to is compatible with one this agent implements: none of the documents is used (§3.1, §3.4).
A version's document on another host is not used: any domain's poppy.json could otherwise link to a file uploaded to a Company's domain (§3.4).
A redirect from a version's document is not followed (§3.4).
A version's document whose protocol_version is not the version it is listed under is not used (§3.4).
A version's document has no supported_versions of its own: one that lists more is not used (§3.4).
Every document a Company serves has the same organization.domain and selects the same issuer: a version's document naming another issuer is not used (§3.4).
A request with the Session header and no Poppy-Version is version_unsupported, HTTP 400 with a JSON body (§3.4).
A request whose Poppy-Version is compatible with no version the company serves is version_unsupported, and is not handled under another version (§3.4).

Each version poppy.json lists in supported_versions has its document at an HTTPS URL on the same host, with that protocol_version, no supported_versions, the same organization.domain and issuer (§3.4); nothing to check when none is listed.
web.disabled asks Personal Agents not to browse: the Company lists its agent or APIs and no browser_session_endpoint (§6).
A Company that sets web.disabled MUST NOT list browser_session_endpoint (§6).
A Company that sets web.disabled MUST list agent or apis (§6).
web.unscoped says poppy:browser-sign-in gives the account's full access on the website; the scope is requested only from a Company that lists browser_session_endpoint (§6).
A Company that sets web.unscoped MUST list browser_session_endpoint (§6).
A request that does not declare operations gets extension_required (403) from a channel that would propose one, never an operation (§3.3, Operations 2).
A company that lists feedback needs no issuer (§3.2): a domain without protected resource metadata is one with none.
Every URL the protocol defines is HTTPS, the tasks endpoint included (§3, §3.1).
A company that lists excluded tasks, publishes skills or takes feedback lists tasks.endpoint in poppy.json (§3.1, §9); feedback, excluded_tasks and skill_index are no longer read from it.

GET {tasks.endpoint} with the Session header and no access token answers 200 with the tasks response (excluded_tasks, skill_index, feedback), which poppy.json no longer carries; a Session header that fails its checks is invalid_session (§9).
A feedback report with a Session Token and no scope is accepted with 202, a kind the company doesn't recognize too; a task over 200 characters is invalid_request; without a token it is 401.
Poppy-Extensions is an RFC 9651 List of Strings with the version in v; a header that fails to parse, or an item without a version, declares nothing (§3.4).

A Company that lists the UCP extension serves its UCP profile at https://{organization.domain}/.well-known/ucp with no redirect; identity linking's scopes are in scopes_supported, and with sign-in it offers Direct Sign-In and private_key_jwt (UCP extension 2 to 4); skipped when it doesn't list the extension.
